chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a Magian woman who embraced Islam before her husband had sexual intercourse with her. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to her husband: 'Embrace Islam.' But her husband refused to embrace Islam. So he judged for her that upon him is half the dower, and said: 'Islam has not increased her except in honor.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's dower if she converts to Islam before consummation and her husband refuses to convert?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that religious incompatibility, specifically when the wife converts and the husband remains a Magian, constitutes valid grounds for dissolution even before consummation. The Imam’s declaration that Islam brought her 'honor' (izz) rather than loss underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the wife’s independent faith status can necessitate separation if the husband refuses to join her, prioritizing spiritual integrity over marital continuity. This precedent is frequently cited in discussions of khula' and mutual consent in mixed-faith unions within Shia fiqh.
